title: Jolly Josh welcomes Rochdale families with inclusive play, music and activity sessions
excerpt: The Castleton charity is reaching out to families caring for children and young people with complex medical needs and physical disabilities, with weekly sessions and bookable activities.
body:
Rochdale charity Jolly Josh is reaching out to families caring for children and young people with complex medical needs and physical disabilities, with a programme of inclusive activities and support.

Based at 2 Ensor Mill in Castleton, Rochdale, OL11 2NU, the centre welcomes children and young adults aged from birth to 19.

The charity says finding activities where a child is welcomed, understood and supported can be difficult, and wants more parents, carers, relatives and professionals to know what is available.

Its programme includes music and signing, themed play sessions, an after-school club, a youth group and activities that families can book directly with the centre.

Weekly sessions

Sing And Sign runs every Wednesday from 10.30am to 12.30pm, bringing together music, songs and signing to make communication fun.

Themed Stay And Play takes place every Tuesday and Saturday from 9.30am to 12.30pm. Sessions offer activities, friendship and a different theme each week.

Sensory Touch And Music runs every Thursday from 10am to noon, offering a relaxing sensory session.

The After School Club takes place every Wednesday from 4pm to 7pm, with inclusive activities and a light tea offered for every child.

The Youth Group meets every Thursday from 5pm to 8pm, giving young people a welcoming space to socialise, take part in activities and build friendships.

Activities available to book

Hydrotherapy sessions can be booked for families or with the centre’s Hydro Lead.

Private sound bath sessions are also available by contacting the centre, offering an opportunity to take time out of a busy schedule.

Rebound Therapy provides supported movement and sensory experiences using a trampoline, with sessions bookable through the centre.

How to get in touch

Parents, carers, family members and professionals supporting a child with complex medical needs are invited to contact Jolly Josh to learn more about its sessions.

Call 01706 399141, email sarah@jollyjosh.co.uk or visit https://jollyjosh.co.uk/

The centre asks anyone planning to visit to contact the team first so an appointment can be arranged.

Families can contact the centre to discuss which sessions suit their child and ask about booking, availability and charges.

The charity is also encouraging people to share its appeal with families who may not yet know about the support available.

Source: Jolly Josh session information supplied to Rochdale Daily; centre details confirmed through https://jollyjosh.co.uk/
